findings.highlight: I might decide on this hair…
findings.evidenceJa: 天才ピアニスト冬馬曜子の最高傑作は何かと聞かれたら、俺なら、この髪とその持ち主だと断言するくらい…
findings.explanation: Asked for Youko's greatest masterpiece, Haruki would unhesitatingly name both this hair and its owner—Kazusa herself. The English names only the hair, dropping the central declaration that Kazusa is Youko's supreme creation.
findings.japanese:
天才ピアニスト冬馬曜子の最高傑作は何かと聞かれたら、
俺なら、この髪とその持ち主だと断言するくらい…
findings.todokanai: If someone were to ask me what Touma Youko's greatest masterpiece was, I might decide on this hair…

findings.highlight: But Kazusa was very slightly hurt by my question that conveyed that I had an unimaginable attachment to her.
findings.evidenceJa:
けれどかずさは、
俺の、かつてないくらいかずさ寄りの問いかけにも、
ほんの少し傷ついた。
findings.explanation: Haruki's question is unprecedentedly aligned with Kazusa's side; 'unimaginable attachment' changes stance into emotional intensity — His willingness to let her skip practice for him remains.
findings.japanese:
けれどかずさは、
俺の、かつてないくらいかずさ寄りの問いかけにも、
ほんの少し傷ついた。
findings.todokanai: But Kazusa was very slightly hurt by my question that conveyed that I had an unimaginable attachment to her.

findings.highlight: And I accept that slight bit of unreasonableness in Kazusa.
findings.evidenceJa: そして俺は、かずさのそんな小さな理不尽に、胸を掻きむしられる。
findings.explanation: Kazusa's small, unreasonable hurt claws or tears at Haruki's heart. The English says he accepts her unreasonableness, replacing an involuntary wound with calm accommodation just before his embrace becomes crushingly desperate.
findings.japanese:
そして俺は、かずさのそんな小さな理不尽に、
胸を掻きむしられる。
findings.todokanai: And I accept that slight bit of unreasonableness in Kazusa.

findings.highlight: "You don't have to be in such a rush. Until March, there are countless places in Japan with lots of snow."
findings.evidenceJa:
「別に慌てなくても大丈夫。
三月いっぱいまでなら、雪が積もってるところなんか、
日本にはいくらでもある」
findings.explanation: Snow remains through the end of March, not merely until March begins — Kazusa still hears the intended extension beyond their two-week limit.
findings.japanese:
「別に慌てなくても大丈夫。
三月いっぱいまでなら、雪が積もってるところなんか、
日本にはいくらでもある」
findings.todokanai: "You don't have to be in such a rush. Until March, there are countless places in Japan with lots of snow."

findings.highlight: no matter how big the difference in our body temperatures becomes
findings.evidenceJa: けれど俺は、徐々に広がる温度差を感じていながらも、そこで言葉を切る器用さを持ち合わせていなかった。
findings.explanation: Haruki senses the figurative temperature gap widening between his feverish fantasy of future seasons together and Kazusa's cooling, lonely response. The English makes it a difference in their literal body temperatures, breaking the scene's emotional thermometer.
findings.japanese:
けれど俺は、徐々に広がる温度差を感じていながらも、
そこで言葉を切る器用さを持ち合わせていなかった。
findings.todokanai: But no matter how big the difference in our body temperatures becomes, I can't stop myself from speaking.

findings.highlight: the joy I had expected from her at that moment
findings.evidenceJa: けれど、その時得られるはずの喜びは、自分だけが感じられる、自分だけの心の動き。
findings.explanation: The joy Haruki imagines obtaining if Kazusa stays is an emotion only he would feel—his private self-satisfaction. The English says he expected joy from Kazusa, changing whose response was anticipated and blurring why she compares his demand with asking him to abandon Japan.
findings.japanese:
けれど、その時得られるはずの喜びは、
自分だけが感じられる、自分だけの心の動き。
findings.todokanai: However, the joy I had expected from her at that moment was something that only I felt, something that only I felt moved by.

findings.highlight: even Kazusa, who has never beaten me in an argument before
findings.evidenceJa: そんな拙い理屈だから、今まで言い合いで負けたことのないかずさにも、こんなにあっさりと論破されてしまう。
findings.explanation: Kazusa has never lost an argument; even she can effortlessly refute reasoning this poor. The English says she has never beaten Haruki, reversing her established argumentative dominance and contradicting the fact that she has just shattered his case.
findings.japanese:
そんな拙い理屈だから、
今まで言い合いで負けたことのないかずさにも、
こんなにあっさりと論破されてしまう。
findings.todokanai: My reasoning is so awkward that even Kazusa, who has never beaten me in an argument before, can completely shatter it.

findings.highlight: causing both to break down without a sound
findings.evidenceJa: あり得ない前提に、あり得ない前提をぶつけられ、ぐうの音も出ないほどに、叩き潰されて…
findings.explanation: Kazusa counters Haruki's impossible premise with another impossible premise, crushing Haruki so completely that he cannot make a sound. The English says the two suggestions themselves both collapse, erasing Kazusa's victory and the pressure that nearly forces Haruki to consider leaving Japan.
findings.japanese:
あり得ない前提に、
あり得ない前提をぶつけられ、
ぐうの音も出ないほどに、叩き潰されて…
findings.todokanai: An impossible suggestion collides with the impossible suggestion made before it, causing both to break down without a sound…

findings.highlight: I scrapped all of the articles that were written about it back then.
findings.evidenceJa: 「…存じてます。その時の記事、スクラップしてありますから。休暇を反対されたときに突きつけようと思って」
findings.explanation: Miyo has clipped and saved the old articles in a scrapbook so she can confront Youko with them if denied leave. In ordinary English, 'scrapped all of the articles' means discarded or destroyed them, contradicting the very blackmail joke in the next sentence.
findings.japanese:
「…存じてます。
その時の記事、スクラップしてありますから。
休暇を反対されたときに突きつけようと思って」
findings.todokanai: "…I'm aware of it. I scrapped all of the articles that were written about it back then. I intended to blackmail you with them in case you refused me my holiday."

findings.highlight: …I wonder what she finds so amusing about this. This is obviously going to be a crappy performance with absolutely no potential for improvement.
findings.evidenceJa:
…何がそんなに楽しいのやら。
想像通りの、全然成長の後が見られない
下手くそな演奏に決まってるのに。
findings.explanation: Haruki expects no sign of growth since his old playing; 'no potential for improvement' changes retrospective stagnation into future incapacity — He still anticipates an unchanged bad performance.
findings.japanese:
…何がそんなに楽しいのやら。
想像通りの、全然成長の後が見られない
下手くそな演奏に決まってるのに。
findings.todokanai: …I wonder what she finds so amusing about this. This is obviously going to be a crappy performance with absolutely no potential for improvement.

findings.highlight: With the way I am now, I've denied every single one of them.
findings.evidenceJa: その一つ一つのどれもが、今の俺の全てを否定する。
findings.explanation: Every remembered word from Haruki's confession and Setsuna's answer denies or condemns everything he is now. The English makes present Haruki the agent who has denied the memories, reversing the moral judgment that makes his hand freeze on Kazusa's song.
findings.japanese:
その一つ一つのどれもが、
今の俺の全てを否定する。
findings.todokanai: With the way I am now, I've denied every single one of them.

findings.highlight: that feeling, and that way she lets me spoil her
findings.evidenceJa: 何度触れても、どれだけ重なっても、飽きることのない光景と匂いと息遣いと感触、そして、甘さだった。
findings.explanation: Following the explicit mention of all five senses, Haruki lists sight, scent, breath or sound, touch, and finally sweetness or taste. The English turns the culminating taste into Kazusa letting him spoil her, breaking the sensory enumeration and inventing an interpersonal behavior.
findings.japanese:
何度触れても、どれだけ重なっても、
飽きることのない光景と匂いと息遣いと感触、
そして、甘さだった。
findings.todokanai: No matter how many times I touch her, no matter how many times I press against her, I can never get tired of that look, that scent, that breath, that feeling, and that way she lets me spoil her.

findings.highlight: Though we did attempt to run away just a little bit.
findings.evidenceJa: ほんの少しのいたたまれなさを除いては。
findings.explanation: Their desired day was complete except for a small residue of unbearable awkwardness after someone nearly discovered them. The English invents an attempt to run away, an action that did not occur, and misstates the emotional exception prompting Kazusa to question staying in Haruki's room.
findings.japanese: ほんの少しのいたたまれなさを除いては。
findings.todokanai: Though we did attempt to run away just a little bit.
